0c21a9c40f.q: Why did Jessica Velazquez Schlegel leave teaching in 2017?
0c21a9c40f.a: Jessica left teaching in 2017 when she had triplets, one of whom has mild cerebral palsy called hemiplegia. The cost of finding a nanny combined with the need for intensive therapies and specialist appointments would have consumed her entire teaching salary, leaving only a couple hundred dollars. She chose to stay home to be present at therapies and specialist doctor appointments for her family, which was the most viable option financially and emotionally.

846b5a4896.q: What specific incident prompted Jessica Velazquez Schlegel's viral social media post about teaching?
846b5a4896.a: Jessica posted about being denied comp time to attend her eighth-grade daughter's moving-up ceremony. She had earned comp time by writing another teacher's IEPs, but her principal refused the request even though that day was a mandatory snow make-up day with no students present—the entire staff spent eight hours in their classrooms doing nothing before summer break. This represented the breaking point of feeling unsupported as both a professional educator and a parent.

b807701192.q: How has teaching changed since COVID according to Jessica Velazquez Schlegel?
b807701192.a: Jessica observed that COVID drastically changed teaching by eliminating grace and comp time for teachers. Districts stopped allowing teachers to bring their children into buildings after hours, removed flexibility around family emergencies, and increased demands for instant responses to parent emails at all hours. She also noted a significant shift in technology expectations, with teachers now expected to monitor district emails and apps on personal cell phones 24/7, leading to increased teacher burnout.

e4ab582946.q: What do employers misunderstand about working mothers in schools according to Play Lab founder Jessica Velazquez Schlegel?
e4ab582946.a: Jessica emphasized that employers don't understand working mothers need to care for their own sick children. When her building was criticized for staff absences, she pushed back requesting data on how many staff were parents of young children in daycare, noting that daycare is a petri dish where children constantly catch illnesses—a reality employers seemed to disregard when assessing attendance records.

3af11cb70e.q: Why does Jessica Velazquez Schlegel refuse to put district apps on her personal cell phone?
3af11cb70e.a: Jessica refuses to install district email or apps on her personal cell phone because the school does not pay for her personal device. She will not accept notifications at 5pm, 6pm, or 10pm, nor will she respond to parent inquiries about assignments or test scores outside work hours. She views her personal time and family time as sacred and non-negotiable, a boundary she believes all educators should protect.
